title: Hash Update-after-Final silently reinitialises context
description:
In crypto2dev_hash(), the Final path (info->hash.digest != NULL) frees devCtx and sets *devctx_ptr = NULL (lines 956-959). A subsequent Update call finds *devctx_ptr == NULL and enters the init-new-context branch (line 895), silently starting a fresh hash over the new data.

Trigger: caller calls wc_Sha256Update() after wc_Sha256Final() on the same wc_Sha256 object with a hardware devId.
Outcome: the subsequent Update produces wrong hash output (hash of only the post-Final data, not an error). wolfSSL's wc_Sha256GetHash also calls Final path; a wc_Sha256Update after wc_Sha256GetHash would be silently wrong.

Note: wolfSSL typically Init()s before re-use, so normal TLS code paths do not hit this. Still a latent correctness hazard for direct API users.

Fix: on entry to crypto2dev_hash(), if info->hash.in != NULL (Update) and *devctx_ptr == NULL, distinguish between 'never inited' and 'already finaled'. One approach: return BAD_FUNC_ARG for Update with no active context (0-length Update is a no-op but nonzero Update without prior Init is an API misuse).
notes: Deferred: fix requires a sentinel value (e.g. FINALIZED_SENTINEL = (void*)(-1)) in devctx_ptr to distinguish never-inited from already-finalized. Design decision needed before implementing.
